PyFixest 0.70 moves the state of a fitted model out of loose private attributes
such as `fit._se`, `fit._vcov`, or `fit._X` into typed components: `fit.model`,
`fit.options`, `fit.sample_info`, `fit.coeftable`, `fit.variance_covariance`,
`fit.fitstat`, `fit.sandwich`, `fit.first_stage`, and others. Each component is
documented in the [API reference](/reference/index.qmd).

Code written against PyFixest 0.60 keeps working while you migrate:

- Most 0.60 names are **deprecated aliases**. They return the value PyFixest
  0.60 returned and emit a `PyfixestDeprecationWarning` that names the
  replacement.
- A few 0.60 values cannot be rebuilt exactly. Their names are **removed**:
  reading them raises an `AttributeError` that explains why and names the
  replacement.
- `fit._u_hat` is not covered yet. On weighted OLS and IV fits it returns,
  without a warning, the unweighted residuals that `fit.resid()` returns,
  where 0.60 multiplied them by the square root of the weights.

```{python}
import warnings

import pyfixest as pf
from pyfixest.errors import PyfixestDeprecationWarning

data = pf.get_data()
fit = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1", data, vcov={"CRV1": "f1"})

with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
    warnings.simplefilter("always")
    old = fit._se

print(caught[0].message)
print((old == fit.coeftable.se).all())
```

## Find the old names in your code

`PyfixestDeprecationWarning` is a `FutureWarning`, so Python shows it by
default. To find every place that still reads a deprecated name, turn the
warning into an error, for example in your test suite:

```{python}
#| eval: false
warnings.simplefilter("error", PyfixestDeprecationWarning)
```

With pytest, add `"error::pyfixest.errors.PyfixestDeprecationWarning"` to the
`filterwarnings` setting instead.

## Values that differ from the new components

The deprecated names return what PyFixest 0.60 returned. For the names below,
that value differs from the new field named in the warning and in the "Use
instead" column, for example `fit._X` versus `fit.within_data.design`:

- **Weighted arrays.** PyFixest 0.60 stored the arrays of weighted OLS and IV
  fits multiplied by the square root of the weights (`_Y`, `_X`, `_Z`,
  `_X_hat`, `_v_hat`, `_sumFE`), and the final IRLS arrays of GLMs multiplied
  by the square root of the working weights (`_Y`, `_X`, `_Z`, `_u_hat`, and
  `_sumFE` of weighted fits). The aliases apply the same scaling. The new components hold the unweighted
  arrays: `fit.within_data`, `fit.working_state`, `fit.first_stage`, and
  `fit.fixef_estimates`.
- **Empty defaults.** PyFixest 0.60 set many attributes to an empty array,
  `None`, or `NaN` before it computed them. An alias raises `AttributeError`
  until its component is published instead, for example `fit._alpha` before
  `fit.fixef()` runs or `fit._eff_F` before `fit.IV_Diag()` runs.
- **Lists instead of tuples.** `_icovars` and `_clustervar` return a list or
  `None`, `_collin_index` returns an empty list when no column was dropped, and
  `_G` repeats the smallest cluster count three times under the default
  `ssc(G_df="min")`.
- **Canonical formulas.** `_fml` and `_model_name` return the canonical
  formula PyFixest now stores, such as `Y ~ 1 + X1`; `_fixef` joins the fixed
  effects with `+` and no spaces.
- **Changed support.** `_support_crv3_inference` reports that non-Poisson GLMs
  no longer accept CRV3 inference. `did2s()` fits report their cluster
  variable in `_vcov_type`, `_clustervar`, `_is_clustered`, and `_G`.

## Names still read by other packages

Released versions of [marginaleffects](https://github.com/vincentarelbundock/pymarginaleffects)
and [maketables](https://github.com/py-econometrics/maketables) read some of
these names directly. Those aliases return their value without a warning until
both packages read the new components; the table marks them as silent.

## All deprecated names

"Model classes" names the classes whose fits the row applies to; subclasses
follow their parent, so a `Feols` row also covers IV, GLM, and quantile fits
unless a later row names them.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from pyfixest.estimation.models._deprecated_attributes import (
    DEPRECATED_ATTRIBUTES,
    Removed,
)

print("| Old attribute | Model classes | Use instead | Status |")
print("|---|---|---|---|")
for attribute in DEPRECATED_ATTRIBUTES:
    for class_name, entry in attribute.classes.items():
        if isinstance(entry, Removed):
            status = f"Removed: {entry.reason}"
        else:
            status = "Deprecated alias" + (" (silent)" if attribute.silent else "")
        print(
            f"| `fit.{attribute.name}` | `{class_name}` "
            f"| `{entry.replacement}` | {status} |"
        )
```
